name: Ciompi Revolt
summary: In July 1378, the wool-workers (ciompi) of Florence, the lowest guild workers, excluded from political representation, revolt against the city's guild oligarchy. Led by a wool carder named Michele di Lando, they seize the Palazzo della Signoria and establish a brief worker-led government (July–September 1378). Three new guilds are created for previously unrepresented workers. The oligarchic guilds unite to suppress the rebellion; within three months the ciompi guilds are dissolved. The revolt is the most radical popular uprising in 14th-century Italy and directly influences political theory on popular sovereignty.

_quarry.structural_significance: First major artisan-class uprising in medieval European city politics; brief experiment in worker governance decades before equivalent European movements; stimulates debates about guild representation and popular sovereignty that influence later political thought
